solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Retreats without black jackets

indicators.note: without tells us to take the black letter away from the jackets

parts.note: Barbours are waxed country jackets, named after the British maker
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Someone describes a holiday or getaway where nobody bothered to bring their dark coats.
explanation.walkthrough: A Barbour is a waxed cotton jacket by a British brand, much worn in the countryside; drop the B and the jackets become garden shelters.
explanation.definitionFit: Shady garden bowers are places to withdraw to, so they are retreats in the sense of secluded refuges.

clue.text: Manoeuvres suggested by Mary

parts.note: the phrase in the answer read as wordplay says the letters of army are exercised, i.e. shuffled, giving this name

explanation.surface: A woman named Mary proposes military drills.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer read as an instruction (stir up the letters of ARMY) produces the name in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Military training operations in the field are called manoeuvres, especially large-scale ones.

clue.text: Titled fellow, one replaced by representative old northern idiot

indicators.note: replaced by says the word one is swapped out for the pieces that follow

parts.note: a baronet holds a hereditary title
an MP is a Member of Parliament, an elected representative

explanation.surface: A titled man stands down in favour of an elected old-timer from the north who is a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replaced by' swaps the letters of 'one' out of the title for the MP and O pieces. The answer is Lancashire and Yorkshire dialect, hence 'northern'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Lancashire and Yorkshire dialect word for a fool, so an idiot in the speech of northern England.

clue.text: Immense interest in American panel dismissing judge

indicators.note: dismissing means the judge's letter is sent out of the panel

parts.note: a jury is a panel deciding a case

explanation.surface: A US jury sends its judge away, with huge public curiosity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interest' looks like attention but is money charged on a loan.
explanation.definitionFit: Lending at exorbitant rates charges excessive money on loans, so enormous interest on debt.

clue.text: Mushy pea tarts practising social distancing

indicators.note: mushy peas are mashed, so the letters of pea tarts are mashed together

explanation.surface: Soggy pastries keep their distance from each other, in pandemic language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mushy pea' looks like the British dish of mashed marrowfat peas, but 'Mushy' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping oneself separate from others, isolated and apart, is what social distancing involves.

clue.text: River goes past university quarter

indicators.note: a river flowing past a place wraps round it here, so the river's letters enclose the other piece

parts.note: the Forth is a Scottish river

explanation.surface: A river flows by a campus, a pleasant riverside image.
explanation.walkthrough: The Forth is the river that flows into the Firth of Forth at Edinburgh.
explanation.definitionFit: One of four equal parts is a fourth, exactly the same fraction as a quarter.

clue.text: Force probably on the ground or up in the air

parts.note: F is the usual abbreviation for force, for instance in physics
lying down means lying on the ground

explanation.surface: A puzzle about where some force will end up: on land or airborne.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the ground or up in the air' looks like two alternatives; only the second is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Travelling through the sky is being up in the air, airborne like a bird.

clue.text: Indigestible French article on a piece of furniture

parts.note: une is the feminine French indefinite article
a table is a piece of furniture

explanation.surface: A French news story about food that disagrees with you sits on a table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'article' looks like a newspaper piece but is the grammatical article.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that cannot be eaten is not fit to digest, so inedible or indigestible.

clue.text: Capital with power to stop small group initially living independently

indicators.note: to stop means to plug, so the power letter fills a gap inside the group

parts.note: a trio is a small group of three

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of each of the two words

explanation.surface: A capital city where a small faction, with power, keeps others from living freely.
explanation.walkthrough: P goes inside TRIO to give TRIPO, then L and I follow.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the chief city of Libya, its seat of government, i.e. a national capital.

clue.text: Quarter gets messed up in gracious woodwork

indicators.note: in places the shuffled letters within the exclamation

parts.note: 'my!' and 'gracious!' are both exclamations of surprise

indicators.note: messed up says the letters of the word quarter are jumbled

explanation.surface: Part of a town is in disarray amid its graceful wooden craftsmanship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gracious' looks like an adjective describing the woodwork but is the exclamation, as in 'goodness gracious!'; 'gets messed up' shuffles the fodder to ARQUETR.
explanation.definitionFit: This is inlaid veneer work in wood, a decorative kind of woodwork used on furniture.

clue.text: Caught inside, backing current order

indicators.note: inside says the caught letter sits within the other piece
backing means the word for current is read backwards

parts.note: a tide is a current of the sea
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A cricket commentary: a batsman caught, a team backing the current batting order.
explanation.walkthrough: TIDE reversed by 'backing' is EDIT, and the C goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A decree issued by authority is an official order or command.

clue.text: A quarter there knew ties need breaking

indicators.note: breaking the words there knew ties lets their letters be rearranged

explanation.surface: Somebody already knew that certain bonds had to be broken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A quarter' is a quarter of a year.
explanation.definitionFit: A year is fifty-two weeks, so a fourth of it, a three-month period, is this span.

clue.text: Quarter of Arabian Desert has space with Australian company

parts.note: an em is a printer's unit of space
Pty is the abbreviation in Australian company names for proprietary

explanation.surface: An Australian firm stakes out room in a remote corner of the Arabian desert.
explanation.walkthrough: The Rub' al Khali in Arabia is known in English as the Empty Quarter; the definition is a fill-in-the-blank.
explanation.definitionFit: The vast sandy Rub' al Khali is called the Empty Quarter, so this word names that region of desert.

clue.text: Greek god and alien change into cakes

parts.note: Pan is the Greek god of the wild
ET is the film alien, the extra-terrestrial

indicators.note: change tells us the letters of the word into are rearranged

explanation.surface: A god and an extra-terrestrial transform themselves into baked goods, a mythological fantasy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' gives TONI; the answer is the Italian plural, so 'cakes' is plural too.
explanation.definitionFit: These are Italian sweet breads eaten at Christmas, a type of cake; this is the Italian plural.

clue.text: Some tempting logs I see inside

indicators.note: inside puts the sound of I see within the word for logs

parts.note: to log data is to enter it, so logs means enters
IC said aloud is 'I see'

explanation.surface: Something about appealing logs one notices within, perhaps a tempting fireside.
explanation.walkthrough: IC is a crossword way of writing 'I see', read as letters. 'Some tempting' is a plural noun phrase: some people who tempt.
explanation.definitionFit: People who lure or seduce others are tempters, so some folk doing the tempting are these.

clue.text: Ethnic quarter feature, one keeping two busy

parts.note: the chin is a facial feature

indicators.note: keeping says the word for one holds the other piece

parts.note: an means one, as in 'an apple'

indicators.note: busy suggests the letters of two are in motion and rearranged

explanation.surface: A distinctive feature of a district, one place keeping a pair occupied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'busy' shuffles the fodder to TOW, and 'keeping' puts that inside the word for one.
explanation.definitionFit: Many cities have a district settled by Chinese communities, an urban ethnic enclave like this.

clue.text: Player's boot is undone

definitions.note: read as 'player is': the definition is the musician, and the 's is the link

indicators.note: undone means the letters are unpicked and reassembled

explanation.surface: A footballer's boot has come untied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Player' suggests a footballer beside 'boot', but it is a musician; the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who plays the oboe in an orchestra is a woodwind performer, a kind of musical player.

clue.text: Bill judge a small sum at close quarters

parts.note: an ad is a bill, a poster advertising something
a cent is a small sum of money

explanation.surface: Someone named Bill judges a trivial amount of money up close.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a name but is a poster, an advertisement.
explanation.definitionFit: Things next to each other are near, side by side, so close by in position.

clue.text: Evacuated Coventry cathedral with body of mice coming round regularly

indicators.note: evacuated means emptied, so only the outside letters of each word remain
the body of a word is its inside, leaving out the first and last letters

explanation.surface: Coventry Cathedral emptied, with mice running about inside: a picture of a deserted church.
explanation.walkthrough: Coventry Cathedral, bombed in 1940, is famous in England.
explanation.definitionFit: Something recurring in cycles happens again and again at intervals, i.e. keeps returning periodically.

clue.text: Study archdeacon starting tombola in religious quarters

parts.note: to con is to study a text
Ven, the Venerable, is the title of an archdeacon

indicators.note: starting picks the first letter of the word tombola

explanation.surface: A churchman studies, starting a raffle at a nunnery.
explanation.walkthrough: A tombola is a British raffle with prizes drawn from a drum, usual at church fetes. An archdeacon is addressed as 'the Venerable'.
explanation.definitionFit: A building where nuns live together is a home for those in religious orders.

clue.text: Central part of hedge is eaten by sheep going sideways

indicators.note: the central part of a word is all but its ends
eaten by says the other piece sits inside the sheep

parts.note: a ewe is a female sheep

explanation.surface: Sheep nibble the middle of a hedge as they move along it sideways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is eaten by' reads naturally in the surface, but the 'is' supplies its own two letters, which go inside the sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving with the edge foremost is going sideways rather than face on, the same direction.

clue.text: Maybe Netanyahu is regularly treated with lithium

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter of the word treated

parts.note: Li is the chemical symbol for lithium

explanation.surface: A politician being routinely given lithium as medication.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the even letters of 'treated'. 'Maybe' marks Netanyahu as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Benjamin Netanyahu is a prime minister of Israel, so one example of a citizen of that country.

clue.text: May look up advanced American oil

parts.note: may and can both express permission

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word for look is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: lo is an old word for look
A is the abbreviation for advanced, as in A level

explanation.surface: Someone may check on an advanced US oil product.
explanation.walkthrough: 'May' looks like the month or a name but is the verb 'can'.
explanation.definitionFit: This rapeseed product is the North American name for a cooking oil from rapeseed.

clue.text: Christmas visitor, any stupid American philosopher

parts.note: Santa Claus visits on Christmas Eve

indicators.note: stupid suggests the letters of the word any are muddled

explanation.surface: Father Christmas is called a foolish American thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stupid' scrambles the fodder to YAN.
explanation.definitionFit: George Santayana was a Spanish-American thinker and writer, a philosopher known for 'those who cannot remember the past...'.

clue.text: Prison warder put in an impossible position

definitions.meaning: slang for a jailer, a guard in a jail
to leave someone stuck with no way out, cheated or ruined

explanation.surface: A jail guard is placed in a hopeless situation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Screw' is British slang for a prison officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: slang for a jail guard, and the verb meaning to wreck someone's chances, leaving them stuck.

clue.text: Hard, heading for argument

parts.note: concrete that has set is hard
to means heading for, as in 'going to'

explanation.surface: Someone firm-minded spoiling for a row.
explanation.definitionFit: A short fierce quarrel or fight is a dispute, a heated argument.

clue.text: Deal with Durham possibly being closed

parts.note: Durham is a bishop's see, the diocese of a bishop
a door pushed to is closed

explanation.surface: A business deal with the city of Durham might be closed.
explanation.walkthrough: Durham is a cathedral city in north-east England and the seat of a bishop; 'possibly' marks it as one example of a see.
explanation.definitionFit: To attend to or take care of a matter is to handle or deal with it.

clue.text: Yonder covert heretics hide

indicators.note: hide says the letters are concealed within the words covert heretics

explanation.surface: Secret heretics conceal themselves far away.
explanation.definitionFit: Yonder is an old word pointing to something at a distance, meaning in that place there.

clue.text: Verse central to alliance between Pakistan and Zambia

indicators.note: central to says only the middle of the two country names, joined into one run, is kept and the ends dropped

explanation.surface: A treaty between two Commonwealth countries contains a poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alliance between' joins the two names into one run; 'central to' keeps its middle six letters, dropping PAKI and MBIA.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of lines forming a unit of a poem is a stanza, so verse in the sense of a stanza.

clue.text: Fools host outside broadcast in American quarter

indicators.note: a host holds its guest, so the word for fools contains the other piece

parts.note: twits are fools

explanation.surface: Silly presenters front an outdoor TV report from a neighbourhood in the US.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' looks like the containment signal but is part of 'outside broadcast', OB; the container signal is 'host'.
explanation.definitionFit: In US slang a bit is twelve and a half cents, so two of them make the 25-cent coin.
